title: Alto saxophone
summary: No render yet. Open sources give only fragments of an alto saxophone air column (a neck cone, two tone-hole positions and a bell cone, from different or unnamed specimens), so the conical bore, the tone-hole lattice and the fingering chart cannot be built from cited numbers without inventing them.
physics_present: generic fs-duct conical and cylindrical segments, tone-hole side branches and a flanged bell load, the lumped single-reed owner and the physical baffled outlet receiver already run for the clarinet; none has been given this instrument's geometry
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two professional alto saxophone players are retained as player data
physics_missing: measured bore diameter profile along the whole air column
tone-hole positions, diameters and chimney heights, pads and key rise, and a fingering chart
blocked: No published measured alto saxophone air column was found; it needs an owner measurement of a specimen, or the geometry table behind the Buffet Crampon alto study of Petersen and co-authors 2020 from its authors.
